# ballast

[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.23427834.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23427834)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/Sullivanstatistics/ballast/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Sullivanstatistics/ballast/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

ballast keeps a result steady under load. It stress-tests a
pre-specified mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM): the model is
refitted under families of data and analytic perturbations, and every
refit is judged against the pre-specified estimate, confidence interval
and p-value.

``` r

library(ballast)
spec <- stress_spec(mmrm::fev_data, response = "FEV1", subject = "USUBJID", visit = "AVISIT",
                    treatment = "ARMCD", reference = "PBO", covariates = ~ RACE + SEX + FEV1_BL,
                    contrast_visit = "VIS4", covariance = "us",
                    method = "Kenward-Roger", vcov = "Kenward-Roger-Linear")   # SAS DDFM=KR
stress_fit(spec)                                   # the pre-specified analysis, one row
# or from a fitted model / an ADaM BDS: stress_spec_mmrm(fit, reference = "PBO"); stress_spec_adam(adeff, "PARAM1")

cen <- stress_census(spec,
  stress_covariance(spec),                         # us, ar1h, ar1, cs, csh, toep, toeph
  stress_inference(spec),                          # Satterthwaite, KR, linear KR, residual, sandwich, jackknife
  stress_covariates(spec),                         # drop each covariate, drop all
  stress_population(spec, list(female = function(d) d$SEX == "Female")),
  stress_loo(spec, by = "RACE"),                   # leave-one-group-out
  stress_permute(spec, n = 500),                   # re-randomisation p
  stress_tipping(spec, deltas = seq(0, -10, -2)),  # delta-adjusted MI (FCS regression)
  stress_reference(spec),                          # MAR, J2R, CR, CIR reference-based MI
  stress_estimator(spec, random = "SITE"),         # complete cases, GEE independence, ANCOVA, robust ANCOVA, random intercept
  stress_fragility(spec, "significance"),          # smallest subject set whose removal flips significance (greedy)
  stress_weights(spec))                            # equal vs observed-margins LS-mean weighting
summary(cen)          # per-family table: counted, significant, crossed, outside CI, reversed, % of base
stress_verdict(cen)   # robust / sensitive / fragile, with a marginal flag
plot(cen)             # one row per family on the percent-of-base axis
plot_swarm(cen)       # bubble swarm of distinct estimates against the no-difference line, deletions beneath
plot_pstrip(cen)      # leave-one-out p-values on a log axis, the base as a diamond
tp <- stress_tipping(spec, deltas = seq(0, -10, -2))
tipping_point(tp)     # interpolated crossing of alpha
plot_pcurve(tp)       # p-value curve over the shift, anchor and crossing marked
# any continuous data perturbation: stress_curve(spec, values, modify = function(data, value) ...)

# the recommended set, pre-specified, run and reported in one go
plan <- standard_plan(spec, site = "SITE", strata = "SITE", baseline = "BASE", deltas = seq(0, -10, -2))
res <- run_plan(plan, cores = 6)
stress_report(res, dir = "stress")    # Markdown + figures
stress_tables(res, dir = "stress")    # CSV, Word, RTF
stress_html(res, "stress/report.html") # interactive
stress_log(res, "stress/log.json")    # audit trail with the plan hash

# or build your own plan
plan <- stress_plan(spec, loo = list(list(), list(by = "SITE")), tipping = list(deltas = seq(0, -10, -2)),
                    estimator = list(random = "SITE", baseline = "BASE"))
plan                                  # SAP-ready text
res <- run_plan(plan, cores = 6)
stress_report(res, dir = "stress")    # Markdown report with the figures
```

## Design stage

The same test runs before the trial.
[`stress_design()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_design.md)
simulates the planned design over a grid of sample sizes and effect
sizes and reports the **robustness power**, the probability that the
pre-specified analysis is significant *and* classed robust, next to the
conventional power, with the verdict rates among significant results,
the chance that one participant’s removal loses significance, and
optionally the deletion search and the delta-adjustment margin.

``` r

des <- stress_design(n_per_arm = c(50, 75, 100, 150), delta = c(0, 4.5), sigma = 10, rho = 0.6,
                     n_visits = 4, dropout = 0.03, covariance = "ar1h", n_trials = 200, cores = 8)
des          # one row per cell; names the smallest n with robustness power >= 0.8
plot(des)    # power and robustness power against subjects per arm
stress_sap(standard_plan(spec, ...))   # the analysis-plan text, to which the expected rates can be added
```

A trial sized for 80% power expects about a third of its significant
results to be classed sensitive; sizing for a robustness power of 80%
removes most of that. The expected rates go into the statistical
analysis plan so the verdict after unblinding has a pre-registered
comparison.

## Definitions

- **Fragile**: some counted alternative reverses the direction of the
  estimate or lands outside the pre-specified 95% confidence interval.
- **Sensitive**: some counted alternative crosses alpha while keeping
  the direction and staying inside the interval.
- **Robust**: no counted alternative crosses alpha.
- **Marginal** (separate flag): the pre-specified p-value lies near
  alpha.

## Roles

Every row carries `role`: `"sensitivity"` for an analysis that keeps the
estimand and changes an assumption or modelling choice,
`"supplementary"` for one that targets a different estimand (ICH
E9(R1)). Alternative data sets and populations default to supplementary;
everything else to sensitivity. The verdict is reported over all counted
rows and over the sensitivity rows alone.

## Counting rule

Rows that reproduce the pre-specified analysis exactly (`is_base`) are
not counted, and a specification reached by two families (the same
estimate, standard error, degrees of freedom and observation count) is
counted once. Tipping-point grids are searches (`kind = "search"`) and
are not counted; the delta-zero multiple-imputation row is.
Leave-one-out deletions are counted but summarised separately from
alternative analyses (`kind = "deletion"`).

## Conventions

The treatment contrast is an explicit least-squares-mean vector with SAS
`LSMEANS` conventions (class covariates at equal weights, continuous
covariates at their means), evaluated with
[`mmrm::df_1d`](https://openpharma.github.io/mmrm/latest-tag/reference/df_1d.html).
`method = "Kenward-Roger"` with `vcov = "Kenward-Roger-Linear"`
reproduces SAS `DDFM=KR`; `method = "Between-Within"` with
`vcov = "Empirical"` reproduces `EMPIRICAL`. AICc uses the SAS REML
definition. The multiple imputation follows PROC MI (FCS regression
method, `MNAR ADJUST` applied at every draw) and PROC MIANALYZE.

## Status and validation

Version 0.6.1. The engine is a generic rewrite of a program-by-program
validated R port of a SAS robustness package and reproduces that package
cell by cell (seven validation gates, about 1,250 cells including the
full submitted census, deterministic quantities to 1e-6, Monte Carlo
quantities within Monte Carlo error); reference-based imputation agrees
with rbmi on its public antidepressant data. See the validation
vignette. `R CMD check --as-cran` runs on Windows, macOS and Linux on
every push.

## Development

ballast was designed and directed by Adam Sullivan, who specified its
methods, made the design decisions and reviewed every function. Code,
tests and documentation were written with Claude (Anthropic), an AI
coding assistant, which is why commits carry a co-author line.
Correctness does not rest on the tool: the package is validated against
an independent SAS reference analysis on about 1,250 cells and against
rbmi (see the validation vignette), and its tests run on every change.

## Citation

Sullivan AJ (2026). ballast: Stress-Test a Pre-Specified Mixed Model for
Repeated Measures. R package version 0.6.1.
<doi:10.5281/zenodo.23427834>. `citation("ballast")` gives the BibTeX
entry.

# Package index

## Specify

- [`stress_spec()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_spec.md)
  : Define the pre-specified MMRM to stress-test
- [`stress_spec_mmrm()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_spec_mmrm.md)
  : Build a stress spec from a fitted mmrm model
- [`stress_spec_adam()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_spec_adam.md)
  : Build a stress spec from an ADaM basic data structure
- [`spec_update()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/spec_update.md)
  : Modify a stress spec
- [`stress_fit()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_fit.md)
  : Fit one MMRM and return one row

## Perturbation families

- [`stress_covariance()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_covariance.md)
  : Perturbation family: within-subject covariance structure

- [`stress_inference()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_inference.md)
  : Perturbation family: degrees-of-freedom method and variance
  estimator

- [`default_inference()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/default_inference.md)
  :

  Default inference settings for
  [`stress_inference()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_inference.md)

- [`stress_covariates()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_covariates.md)
  : Perturbation family: covariate set

- [`stress_weights()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_weights.md)
  : Perturbation family: least-squares-mean weighting

- [`stress_data()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_data.md)
  : Perturbation family: alternative analysis data sets

- [`stress_population()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_population.md)
  : Perturbation family: analysis population

- [`stress_loo()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_loo.md)
  : Perturbation family: leave-one-out deletions

- [`stress_grid()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_grid.md)
  : Perturbation family: crossed specification grid

- [`stress_permute()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_permute.md)
  : Perturbation family: re-randomisation (permutation) test

- [`stress_tipping()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_tipping.md)
  : Perturbation family: delta-adjusted multiple imputation (tipping
  point)

- [`stress_reference()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_reference.md)
  : Perturbation family: reference-based multiple imputation

- [`stress_estimator()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_estimator.md)
  : Perturbation family: estimator class

- [`stress_fragility()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_fragility.md)
  : Smallest set of subjects whose removal changes the conclusion

- [`stress_curve()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_curve.md)
  : Perturbation family: a curve over a continuous data perturbation

- [`stress_estimand()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_estimand.md)
  : Perturbation family: intercurrent-event strategies (ICH E9(R1))

- [`stress_visits()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_visits.md)
  : Perturbation family: the contrast at every visit

- [`stress_ranktest()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_ranktest.md)
  : Perturbation family: rank tests at the contrast visit

## Census and verdict

- [`stress_census()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_census.md)
  : Assemble a census of perturbations against the base analysis
- [`summary(`*`<stress_census>`*`)`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/summary.stress_census.md)
  : Summarise a census by family
- [`stress_verdict()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_verdict.md)
  : Classify the census: robust, sensitive or fragile, and marginal
- [`tipping_point()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/tipping_point.md)
  : Find where a p-value curve crosses alpha
- [`stress_explain()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_explain.md)
  : Explain why an alternative analysis moved

## Pre-specify, run, report

- [`stress_plan()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_plan.md)
  : Pre-specify a stress test
- [`standard_plan()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/standard_plan.md)
  : The standard stress test
- [`run_plan()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/run_plan.md)
  : Run a pre-specified stress test
- [`run_plans()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/run_plans.md)
  : Run several plans (several endpoints or comparisons) and compare
- [`stress_report()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_report.md)
  : Write a stress-test report
- [`stress_tables()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_tables.md)
  : Write regulatory-style tables and the census
- [`stress_log()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_log.md)
  : Write the run log for an audit trail
- [`stress_html()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_html.md)
  : Interactive HTML report
- [`stress_sap()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_sap.md)
  : Statistical-analysis-plan text for a stress test
- [`mask_ids()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/mask_ids.md)
  : Mask subject identifiers in a census

## Figures

- [`plot(`*`<stress_census>`*`)`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/plot.stress_census.md)
  : Plot a census: one row per family on the percent-of-base axis
- [`plot_swarm()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/plot_swarm.md)
  : Bubble-swarm plot of a census against the no-difference line
- [`plot_pcurve()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/plot_pcurve.md)
  : Plot p-value curves over a continuous perturbation
- [`plot_pstrip()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/plot_pstrip.md)
  : Strip plot of p-values after each deletion
- [`plot_pcdf()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/plot_pcdf.md)
  : Empirical distribution of the p-values across a census

## Design and calibration

- [`stress_design()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_design.md)
  [`print(`*`<stress_design>`*`)`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_design.md)
  : Size a trial for a robust result
- [`plot(`*`<stress_design>`*`)`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/plot.stress_design.md)
  : Plot power and robustness power against the sample size
- [`simulate_trial()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/simulate_trial.md)
  : Simulate a two-arm longitudinal trial
- [`stress_calibrate()`](https://sullivanstatistics.github.io/ballast/reference/stress_calibrate.md)
  : Pre-trial calibration of the stress test
